$comment: Queries that legitimately touch a tenant-scoped table WITHOUT a tenant_id predicate.
PLAN.md 8.2 requires every entry to carry a written reason. Nothing goes in here to
silence a warning -- an entry is a claim that cross-tenant exposure is impossible by
some other means, and that claim has to hold on its own.
Tables with no tenant_id column at all are exempt automatically (the audit derives the
tenant-scoped set from prisma/schema.prisma) and need no entry here. `tenants` is the
only such table: its primary key IS the tenant id.

allow.reason: Lookup by primary key using a user id taken from the already-verified session JWT. The id is not attacker-supplied: it was signed by this server at login. Adding a tenant filter would change behaviour, and the tenant in the session came from the same signed payload.

Login is deliberately cross-tenant: the caller has no session yet, so there is no tenant to scope to. The tenant is DERIVED from the matched row and then signed into the session. This was the pre-existing behaviour and the original code documents it. No row data is returned to the caller -- the response is {ok:true} plus a cookie -- so a wrong match cannot leak another tenant's data; it would simply fail the password check.
Primary-key lookup of the session's own user id (signed JWT) to compare credentials_version. Returns a single integer that is compared, never returned.

Counts rows whose viewer_user_id is the session's own user id, which is itself tenant-bound. Returns only a boolean (count > 0) to the caller, never row content. Matches the pre-existing query, which was also not tenant-scoped.

Writes by primary key to the row this request already authenticated (login rehash) or already resolved through a tenant-scoped token lookup (password reset). The id is server-derived in both cases, never taken from the request body.

allow.source: Prisma relation loading for `include: { <parent>: { select: { name: true } } }` in src/lib/auth.ts and the Batch 2 master routes
allow.reason: How Prisma resolves a to-one relation: a second statement fetching the related rows by PRIMARY KEY, using FK values already present on parent rows that were themselves selected under a tenant_id filter. No request input reaches these ids. PostgREST resolved the equivalent embeds the same way, with no tenant filter, so this is not a regression. The reliance on referential integrity was checked against live across the whole database: 39 FK pairs where both sides are tenant-scoped, zero cross-tenant references. Nothing at the DB level ENFORCES it -- a composite FK including tenant_id would make it structural -- and that is recorded as follow-up in PLAN.md 8.2. Tables are enumerated rather than matched by shape on purpose: a plain findMany({ where: { id: { in: ... } } }) emits identical SQL, so a blanket rule would silently swallow a genuinely missing filter.

allow.source: src/app/api/masters/users/route.ts — include: { users: { select: { id, name } } }, the manager embed
allow.reason: Prisma loading the users self-relation (manager_user_id -> users.id) for the aliased `manager` embed. Same class as prisma-to-one-relation-fetch, kept as its own entry because `users` is queried in many other places and a loose pattern here would be dangerous: the pattern is pinned to the exact id+name projection this embed emits. The manager ids come from rows already selected under tenant_id, and the FK check against live found zero cross-tenant references across all 39 tenant-scoped FK pairs. Note the other id-IN query on users (the scope=manage visibility filter in the same route) DOES carry tenant_id and so is never flagged.
